groups.text: Robots: bot swarm run and MuJoCo on the CAD meshes

runs.name: free motion vs one-line motion (donut)
runs.cfg: same unseen shape and damage (cut off; squashed), repaired by two different runs: left = one-line body model (noise, 30% packet loss; ag_axis_mlph_scales2), right = free motion with ideal dots (ag_eps7_scales2_warm1, 10,000 iterations). The two differ in more than motion (body noise, packet loss, random headings, training length), so this shows the size of the gap, not its cause.

runs.name: swarm run (body model)
runs.cfg: 1,024 bots on an unseen shape (the lizard emoji), body model (assumed, motion limits measured in MuJoCo): one line per bot, noisy sensing, 30% packet loss. Four copies: no damage, cut off, squashed, scrambled; damaged at step 32, then left alone. ag_axis_mlph_scales2.

runs.name: swarm run: donut (a hole)
runs.cfg: same as the lizard run, on an unseen shape (donut (a hole)); body model (assumed), ag_axis_mlph_scales2, damaged at step 32. Cuts and squashes are only partly repaired.

runs.name: swarm run: butterfly
runs.cfg: same as the lizard run, on an unseen shape (butterfly); body model (assumed), ag_axis_mlph_scales2, damaged at step 32. Cuts and squashes are only partly repaired.

runs.name: swarm run: procedural shape, two holes
runs.cfg: same as the lizard run, on an unseen shape (procedural shape, two holes); body model (assumed), ag_axis_mlph_scales2, damaged at step 32. Cuts and squashes are only partly repaired.

runs.name: 6 CAD bots in one world (MuJoCo)
runs.cfg: six microbots on the real CAD meshes, each running the validated one-roll script at its own heading, alternating directions, then rolling back; they collide with each other and the floor. Movement demo only: no controller reacts to neighbours, no self-repair here.

runs.name: roll + quarter-turn gait
runs.cfg: one bot from rest: a roll (left) and the validated turning gait (right); simulation, flat-disc feet
